misconceptions.description: Writing a discussion prompt like "Is AI good or bad?" that asks for an opinion with no decision to make, producing one-line posts
misconceptions.trigger: prompt has no decision, tension, or case for students to engage
misconceptions.feedback: Name a specific decision a teacher would face. A good prompt has a tension to negotiate, not a stance to restate.

misconceptions.description: Asking only for opinion so nothing requires students to cite a course anchor or a case detail
misconceptions.trigger: prompt asks what students think with no evidence requirement
misconceptions.feedback: Require a course anchor and a case detail so the post is grounded, not just felt.

misconceptions.description: Writing a prompt where students post in isolation and never have to engage a peer who reasoned differently
misconceptions.trigger: prompt ends after the first post with no reply requirement
misconceptions.feedback: Require a reply to a peer who chose the opposite call so students engage other reasoning.

misconceptions.description: Adding a generic follow-up such as "What does everyone think?" that reopens opinion instead of pressing on the tension
misconceptions.trigger: facilitator accepts a vague follow-up that drops the named tension
misconceptions.feedback: Reject follow-ups that reopen opinion. Press the same tension or escalate the decision.
